To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
plant cystatins inhibit legumains.
carboxy terminal‐extended phytocystatin are bifunctional cysteine proteinase inhibitors of papain-like and legumain-like proteinases.

(i) some PhyCys inhibit legumain‐ and papain‐like proteinases, (ii) the SNSL carboxy terminal motif is involved in the inhibition, and (iii) this inhibition is essential for the biological function of these PhyCys.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a novel class of cystatin‐like proteinase inhibitors, the PhyCys, that inhibit legumain‐type cysteine proteinase activities.
the identification and characterization of plant cysteine proteinase inhibitors, which are able to inhibit both papain‐like and legumain proteinases.
the discovery of a new function of plant PhyCys as bifunctional inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the carboxy terminal SNSL motif of the PhyCys is responsible for inhibition of papain‐ and legumain/cathepsin L‐like proteinases.
carboxy terminal extensions of PhyCys have a dual inhibitory function on both papain and leguminase cysteine proteinase families.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the PhyCys family is composed of two different types of cysteine proteinase inhibitors: those with a single inhibitory function, which inhibit papain‐like enzymes, and those with a dual inhibitory activity, which are able to inhibit both papain‐like and legumain activities.
the SNSL extension of the PhyCys is a new motif for the inhibition of leguminases and that PhyCys are multifunctional proteinase inhibitors.
PhyCys are bifunctional protein inhibitors, able to inhibit simultaneously papain‐like and legumain like‐cysteine proteinases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
plants have a variety of cystatin‐like inhibitors with different inhibitory properties and functions.
plants have evolved to use a similar mechanism to inhibit two different cysteine proteinase families, papain‐like and legumain.
the PhyCys family of inhibitors is more complex than expected and that PhyCys with carboxy terminal extensions may play an important role in the regulation of legumain activities in plants.
